# Series A activity: Week of October 4, 2026

### There were 44 Series As in the last week that raised a total of $2.2 billion. The average deal size was $50.9 million while the median was $20.0 million.

**Ultra** raised $50 million from Framework Ventures on October 9, 2026. Warehouse packing robots offered as a monthly robots-as-a-service lease. Ultra is based in Brooklyn, NY, United States. Website: www.ultra.tech

### **Three Most Interesting Deals**

**Ultra ($50M from Framework Ventures):** Ultra leases warehouse packing robots under a robots-as-a-service model, so customers pay monthly instead of buying hardware upfront. The Brooklyn company says its machines have already packed more than 500,000 orders, and it is pairing its robot bodies with AI from Physical Intelligence rather than building the full stack alone. The bet is that deployable non-humanoid warehouse robots with recurring revenue will scale faster than flashier humanoid demos.

**TypeSafe AI ($870M from Andreessen Horowitz):** TypeSafe builds machine-native AI models, led by Jev, that output calibrated decisions instead of text so enterprises can automate workflows without LLM token bloat. The $870M Series A at a $7.5B valuation landed weeks after Jev launched, which is an unusually fast jump from product release to mega-round. The interesting question is whether non-text decision models become a durable infrastructure category or stay a single-product moment.

**Atlas Atomics ($400M from General Catalyst):** Atlas Atomics is a stealth nuclear company developing heavy-water reactor technology that avoids reliance on enriched uranium. A $400M Series A at roughly a $1.9B valuation puts serious capital behind an unproven reactor design while the company is still quiet on public product detail. This is less a software story and more a bet that cheaper nuclear hardware can clear the next wave of power demand.
